faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by hours per week (typically 38 for full-time) and then by 52 weeks. For example, $30/hour × 38 × 52 = $59,280 gross per year. Use our timesheet to do this instantly.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and an award rate?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage (from 1 July 2026: $26.44/hour) is the legal minimum for employees not covered by an award. Many industries have award rates that are higher, and casual employees get a 25% loading on top. Check your award or use our pay guides.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on my pay?
faqs.a: Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your salary. For 2026-27, the maximum contribution base is $270,830. Our calculator estimates super as 12% of gross ordinary earnings, not including overtime or allowances.

## Calculate Take Home Pay Australia: From Hourly Rate to Annual Salary

If you want to calculate take home pay Australia, the first step is converting your hourly rate to an annual figure. The standard formula is: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. For full-time employees, we assume a 38-hour week (the ordinary hours under most awards and the National Employment Standards). This gives you your gross annual salary before tax and super.

### The Basic Formula

Annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026) the annual gross is $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,241.44. If you work fewer or more hours adjust the weekly hours accordingly. Our [timesheet](/) lets you enter your exact hours and rate to see the instantly.

### Fortnightly Pay Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your gross weekly pay = hourly rate × hours per week. So fortnightly = (hourly × hours) × 2. For a 38-hour week at $30/week weekly = $1,140 fortnightly = $2,280. This is useful for budgeting between pay cycles.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage each year. From 1 July 2026 it is $26.44 per hour for a full-time employee not covered by award. However most employees are covered by a modern award or enterprise agreement which often set higher minimum rates specific industries and roles. For example a retail employee might have a higher base rate under the General Retail Industry Award. Our [pay guides](/blog) and [reference tables](/data) can help you find the correct award rate for your job.

It important to note that the National Minimum Wage is a floor, not a median. If you are looking for the typical pay for a particular occupation the Australian Bureau of Statistics publishes average weekly earnings. For full-time adult adult ordinary time earnings in May 2026 the average was $2,083.70 per week before tax. That is an average across all industries not the median for your specific job. Use our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page for more context.

### Casual Loading If you are a casual employee you are entitled to a casual loading of 25% on top of the base hourly rate. This compensates for not receiving paid leave. On our [timesheet](/blog). Casual loading also applied to award rates where applicable. See our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page for details.

### Superannuation Paid on Top Super guarantee is currently 12% of your ordinary time earnings paid by your employer on top of your gross salary. It is not deducted from your pay. For 2026–27 the maximum contribution base is $270,830 meaning super only calculated on earnings up to that amount. Our calculator estimates super as 12% of your ordinary earnings (the gross annual figure from the formula) but note that does not include overtime allowances or salary sacrifice. For more on super and packaging visit [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Tax and Take-Home Pay To calculate take home pay Australia you need to deduct income tax and Medicare levy from your gross annual salary. The 2026–27 resident tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200 nil
- $18,200 – $45,000 15% of excess over $18,200 $45,001 – $135,000 $4,020 plus 30% of excess over $135,001 – $190,000 $31,020 plus 37% of excess over $190,000 $190,001+ $51,420 plus 45% of excess over $190,000 Medicare levy generally 2% of your taxable income. Note that the Medicare levy reduction thresholds for singles and families for 2026–27 were not confirmed at the time of this guide; we use the 2025–26 thresholds for estimation purposes. Our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page provides a detailed breakdown.

### Example: National Minimum Wage vs Award Let's compare a full-time employee on the National Minimum Wage ($26.44/hour) with one on a typical award rate of $30/hour (for illustration only; actual award rates vary).

- NMW: $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,241.44 gross. Tax (using 2026-27 rates) = $5,436.22 (approx) Medicare = $1,044.83 net = $45,760.39. Super (12% of ordinary earnings) = $6,268.97 paid on top.
- Award $30: $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280 gross. Tax = $7,284 Medicare = $1,185.60 net = $50,810.40. Super = $7,113.60.

The award employee earns more gross and net and receives higher super. This illustrates why it's important to know your correct award classification. Use our [job pay](/topics/job-pay) resources to find your rate.

### Important Notes This calculator provides an estimate. It assumes the same hourly rate every week no unpaid overtime no penalty rates no allowances no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only paid on top and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP the Medicare levy surcharge and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate not a determination of your pay or tax.

For a precise calculation tailored to your situation consult a professional tax professional or use the ATO's tax estimator. Our [about the timesheet](/about) page explains the methodology in detail.

The tool will show your annual gross fortnightly pay estimated tax Medicare net and super. You can also add casual loading with one click.
